lines: A blank panel you can make any width and any colour, with one hidden jack that makes it flicker
Flickers the panel from a cable; the module treats the signal as bipolar once it goes below 0V, and as 0-10V once it goes above 5.25V, subtracting 5V in that case
Note — the flicker jack is behind the #d medallion at the bottom, and is only there while both Show branding and Brand logo are on; Brand logo comes up off, so a new Null shows no jack
Note — drag the left or right edge to change the width; the drag handle appears when the pointer is over an edge
Note — a Copper or Copper-mini sets this panel's colour only from the right-hand side; the module tests its right-hand neighbour twice and never looks left
Note — Copper sets panel color has to be on here and Share color as Extender on in the Copper; the colour is then kept in the patch, so the Copper can be taken out again
Menu — Palette color — sets the panel colour from a list of named colours
Menu — Background — opens a colour picker for the panel colour, transparency included
Menu — Copper sets panel color — allows a Copper or Copper-mini beside this module to set the panel colour
Menu — Show branding — shows or hides the ring-and-slash mark and the #d medallion
Menu — Brand logo — shows the #d medallion when branding is on, which is also what puts the flicker jack on the panel
Menu — Glow in the dark — the panel keeps its own light when the Rack room brightness is turned down, with a halo scaled by the Rack light bloom setting
Menu — Bright in a dark room — the panel is not dimmed when the Rack room brightness is turned down

pachde-info.notes: All ten of this module's parameters are declared without a widget on the panel; they are driven from the Text options dialog, so no click on the module can reach any of them and none is tagged. Info.cpp:17 configures the vertical alignment parameter with the name "Horizontal alignment", the same string given to the horizontal one on line 14; because neither parameter has a widget, the wrong name never appears as a tooltip.

pachde-imagine.notes: Output index 8 is declared in the header as a test output but its configOutput call is commented out (Imagine.cpp:85) and it has no jack on the panel, so it gets no line and no tag. The manual says the Polarity switch puts the v output at -5V to +5V; the code (Imagine.cpp:396) subtracts 0.5 from a value already scaled 0 to 10, so bipolar gives -0.5V to 9.5V. pachde-copper.notes: The polyphonic output is dead. Copper.cpp:267 writes `auto out = getOutput(POLY_OUT);`, which copies the port by value, and the setChannels and voltage writes that follow land on that copy. The shipped binary agrees: in CopperModule::process the port is loaded onto the stack at 0x3c2c0, the channel count is read back from the stack copy, and the seven voltage stores are gone altogether as dead code, with no write back to the module's outputs. The red, green and blue outputs are only computed while one of R, G, B or poly is patched (Copper.cpp:251); since poly writes nothing, patching poly alone gives nothing anywhere.

lines: Changes the look of the whole rack: alternate rails, transparent panels, plainer knobs and jacks, no screws, hidden empty jacks, hidden lights, and a button that packs the modules into neat rows
Note — none of the buttons on this panel is a parameter, so no click on any of them reaches this help; what each one does is set out below

Note — NOJACK hides every jack with no cable in it, and while they are hidden no new cable can be patched; unplugging a cable leaves that jack visible until the button is used again
Note — DARKNESS hides the lights on every module

Note — the round button at the bottom puts the whole rack back to Rack's normal appearance in one click

pachde-skiff.notes: The Rail Theme menu offers Light, Dark and High Contrast, and res/rails holds -light.vgt, -dark.vgt and -high.vgt, but rails.cpp:13-15 returns the light file from all three accessors, so load_rail_themes loads -light.vgt three times. The shipped binary carries only the string res/rails/-light.vgt, confirming the other two files are never read. This module has no parameters, inputs or outputs at all: every control on the panel is a plain widget, so nothing here can be tagged.

pachde-fancybox.notes: The saturation, lightness and transparency inputs of every colour row do nothing with their own voltage. Fancy::modulate_color (Fancy.cpp:204-219) checks all four jacks of a row for a cable but then calls scaled_voltage(input_id_first) four times, so the hue jack's voltage is added to all four colour parts. The shipped binary agrees: in Fancy::modulate_color the voltage is loaded once from the port at input_id_first times 0x50 and the same register is added to hue, saturation, lightness and alpha. Parameters 23 to 32 (image fitting, grayscale, the image offsets and scale, the background switch, and the four case settings) have no widget on this panel and are driven from the ON•OFF button and the two dialogs, so they get no line and no tag. Parameters 25, 26 and 27, the image X offset, Y offset and scale, are configured with an empty name (Fancy.cpp:19-21), which is why the census shows them nameless.

lines: A 2HP version of FancyBox: the same six background layers with their options in dialogs, and no control voltage inputs
Switches the whole background on and off
Turns the background picture layer on and off
Turns the colour wash layer on and off
Turns the linear gradient layer on and off
Turns the radial gradient layer on and off
Turns the box gradient, the vignette, on and off
Turns the cases layer on and off, drawing a frame and a drop shadow around each unbroken run of modules
Note — nothing is drawn until the background is switched on; every layer stays hidden and the blue lamp stays dark until then
Note — a layer's own check box has to be ticked as well; only the colour wash is ticked on a new module
Note — the picture layer shows nothing until an image file is chosen, whatever the check box says
Note — a colour input is only read while its layer is ticked and that colour's fade is above zero
Note — a fast, full-range signal on these inputs gives flashing results; a bipolar signal through an attenuator, with the knobs set part way, gives a gentler one
Note — only one FancyBox works at a time, counting the mini: a second one added to the patch is drawn greyed out with no controls on it at all
Note — the six layers are drawn one over another in this order: picture, colour wash, linear gradient, radial gradient, vignette, cases
Note — the cases layer draws a frame and a drop shadow around each unbroken run of modules; a module standing on its own gets no case, and a gap of more than 1HP starts a new one
Menu — Keep effects when removed — leaves the background in place after this module is deleted from the patch; the settings are then lost when the patch is unloaded, so save a preset first

Note — every setting other than these switches is in the dialogs behind the hamburger marks, one per layer; those settings have no control on the panel, so no click on the module reaches help for them
Note — the module underneath is the one FancyBox uses, so the same background can be built here; this panel leaves out all 46 control voltage inputs, and none of them can be patched
pachde-mini-fancybox.notes: All 46 inputs and 26 of the 33 parameters have no widget on this panel, so they get no line and no tag: the census lists them because the model is shared with FancyBox. The colour-modulation defect described on the FancyBox entry is in the shared module but cannot be reached from this panel, which has no jacks.

Sets Rack's cable tension, 0% to 100%
Sets Rack's room brightness, 0% to 100%
Sets Rack's light bloom, 0% to 100%
Sets how far the cable opacity input moves the setting, 0% to 100%; it comes up at 0%, so a patched cable does nothing until this is turned up
Sets how far the cable tension input moves the setting, 0% to 100%; it comes up at 0%, so a patched cable does nothing until this is turned up
Sets how far the room brightness input moves the setting, 0% to 100%; it comes up at 0%, so a patched cable does nothing until this is turned up
Sets how far the light bloom input moves the setting, 0% to 100%; it comes up at 0%, so a patched cable does nothing until this is turned up
Moves the cable opacity away from the knob setting, 10% per volt at a full amount, scaled by the small knob beside it and held between 0% and 100%
Moves the cable tension away from the knob setting, 10% per volt at a full amount, scaled by the small knob beside it and held between 0% and 100%
Moves the room brightness away from the knob setting, 10% per volt at a full amount, scaled by the small knob beside it and held between 0% and 100%
Moves the light bloom away from the knob setting, 10% per volt at a full amount, scaled by the small knob beside it and held between 0% and 100%
Note — this module writes Rack's own settings, so the change outlives the patch; the four values it found when it started are put back when it is removed
Note — only one Rui works at a time; a second one added to the patch is drawn greyed out with no controls on it at all
Note — the small round button at the top hides and shows all cables at once, and F6 with the pointer over the module does the same; it is not a parameter, so no click on it reaches this help
Note — the triangle button at the bottom, and F2 with the pointer over the module, stops the module writing the settings; no click on it reaches this help
Note — the settings are read from the knobs about once every 64 samples rather than every sample, so a fast signal on the inputs is sampled coarsely
Menu — Reset — puts the four large knobs back to Rack's default settings and the four amounts to zero
Menu — Fluff — shows or hides the coloured shapes drawn behind the controls

Chooses whether the screen covers the panel only, or the knobs, jacks and displays as well; covering them stops that module from being used
Sets the horizontal position of the guide being edited, -1500 to 1500 pixels; a negative value is measured from the right edge, which is how a right margin is made
Sets the vertical position of the guide being edited, -380 to 380 pixels; a negative value is measured from the bottom edge

Menu — 1/2hp right margin — in the hamburger menu at the end of the template row: adds that ready-made set to the list
Menu — 1/2hp horizontal rules — in the hamburger menu at the end of the template row: adds that ready-made set to the list
Menu — 1/2hp vertical rules — in the hamburger menu at the end of the template row: adds that ready-made set to the list
Menu — 1/2hp ruled grid — in the hamburger menu at the end of the template row: adds that ready-made set to the list
Menu — 10px horizontal rules — in the hamburger menu at the end of the template row: adds that ready-made set to the list
Menu — 10px vertical rules — in the hamburger menu at the end of the template row: adds that ready-made set to the list
Menu — 10px ruled grid — in the hamburger menu at the end of the template row: adds that ready-made set to the list
Menu — 1/2hp striped grid — in the hamburger menu at the end of the template row: adds that ready-made set to the list
pachde-guide.notes: The knobs are not in panel order: left to right the panel reads X, Y, W, R, A, which is parameter index 0, 1, 3, 4, 2. Parameter 2 is the angle switch at the right-hand end and parameter 3 is the width knob in the middle. The module's own right-click menu holds nothing but the theme choices, so it has no line here; everything else is on the hamburger at the end of the template row.

lines: Lays a colour over the panels of the modules in your rack, faded in and out by a button or a cable
Chooses whether the colour goes over the panel only, leaving the knobs and jacks clear, or over the whole module, in which case that module can no longer be used
Sets how long the colour takes to fade in and to fade out, 0 to 10 seconds
Chooses whether the jack above it is read as a trigger that turns the toning on and off, or as a continuous level setting the strength of the colour
A trigger here fades the colour in, and the next one fades it out; with the switch below set to Continuous the voltage sets the strength of the colour instead, 0-10V
Note — no panel is toned until the GO button is pressed, or F2 with the pointer over the module; press again to fade out
Note — with the switch below the jack set to Continuous, the GO button has to be on before the voltage does anything, and the jack is then named Fade amount
Note — which modules are toned is chosen in the hamburger menu at the top; the choice is remembered with the patch
Note — the palette button opens a colour picker for the toning colour, and the transparency of that colour sets the strength: an opaque colour hides the panel altogether
Note — the palette button is not a parameter, so no click on it reaches this help
Note — the GO button and the lamp beside it are not parameters, so no click on them reaches this help
Note — a Copper or Copper-mini on either side can set and animate the toning colour, with Use Copper color turned on here and Share color as Extender turned on in the Copper
Note — the toning lays a widget the size of the panel over each module, which assumes a module is built the usual way; modules that draw their own panels may come out differently
Note — toning shows best on dark panels
Menu — Use Copper color — in the hamburger menu at the top: takes the toning colour from a Copper or Copper-mini standing beside this module
Menu — Tone this PanelTone — in the hamburger menu at the top: includes this module itself among the toned ones
Menu — All — in the hamburger menu at the top: tones every module in the rack
Menu — Selected modules — in the hamburger menu at the top: tones the modules that were selected when this was chosen, and keeps that list until it is chosen again
Menu — Modules in this row — in the hamburger menu at the top: tones every module in the same rack row as this one
Menu — Modules to the left — in the hamburger menu at the top: tones every module to the left in this row
Menu — Continuous modules to the left — in the hamburger menu at the top: tones the unbroken run of modules immediately to the left
Menu — Modules to the right — in the hamburger menu at the top: tones every module to the right in this row
Menu — Continuous modules to the right — in the hamburger menu at the top: tones the unbroken run of modules immediately to the right
Menu — Module to the left — in the hamburger menu at the top: tones the one module immediately to the left
Menu — Module to the right — in the hamburger menu at the top: tones the one module immediately to the right

0.why: PanelTone.cpp:201-204 reads the jack with getVoltage and a SchmittTrigger set to 0.1V and 5V while the switch is on Trigger

pachde-paneltone.notes: The input jack does two different things. On Trigger it is read by a Schmitt trigger at 0.1V and 5V (PanelTone.cpp:201-204); on Continuous the voltage is scaled by 0.1 to set the overlay strength (PanelTone.cpp:386), which makes it a 0-10V control voltage input. It is coloured as a trigger here because that is the setting the module comes up in, and because the maker renames the jack to Go trigger or Fade amount to match (PanelTone.cpp:190-194). The module menu carries nothing but the theme choices, so it has no line here; everything else is on the hamburger at the top of the panel.
